hazard: Lack of timely reporting and registration of food allergy fatalities

promises.quote: the AAI EWG recommended in principle that AAIs should be made available in public locations for use to treat anaphylaxis in unforeseen, critical circumstances, provided suitable safeguards can be implemented to ensure effective and safe use of the AAIs.
promises.summary: Make AAI devices available in public locations like food retail outlets.

concerns.quote: Availability of emergency Adrenaline Auto-injector devices (AAIs) in the Retail food sector
concerns.hazard: absence of emergency adrenaline auto-injectors in food businesses

reports.title: Alexandra Briess: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths
Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The issues within this Prevention of Future Deaths report are predominantly national issues, but I heard at inquest that there is no person with named accountability for allergy services and allergy provision at NHS England, or the Department of Health as a whole
concerns.hazard: lack of named accountability for allergy services and allergy provision

concerns.quote: In my opinion action should be taken to consider establishing a national reporting system which includes timely reporting to local authority and FSA and maintenance of a register of fatalities and their investigations, and consideration be given to investigating the feasibility of wider access to AAIs
concerns.hazard: absence of national reporting system for anaphylaxis

concerns.quote: To establish a robust system of capturing and recording cases of anaphylaxes, and specifically, fatal and near-fatal anaphylaxis... · Such a system could involve, mandatory reporting of anaphylaxis presenting to hospital analogous to the current system for notifiable diseases... by registered medical practitioners have a statutory duty to notify the 'proper officer' at their local council or local health protection team of suspected cases of certain infectious diseases
concerns.hazard: inadequate mandatory reporting of anaphylaxis cases

concerns.quote: Gathering data and using this to research and reduce the risk of future deaths requires funding, and this should be reviewed
concerns.hazard: insufficient funding for national anaphylaxis data collection and research

concerns.quote: Consideration of including contact details for the UKFAR in algorithms used by doctors attempting to resuscitate patients - so that there is a clear requirement for referral to UKFAR in the event of an unsuccessful resuscitation
concerns.hazard: missing integration of UKFAR referral in resuscitation protocols

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the lack of a timely national reporting system and register for allergy-related fatalities, calling for improved information sharing between local authorities, coroners and the FSA.
links.earlier_quote: The Head of Incidents at the FSA informed the court that the FSA has started work on a reporting platform for allergic reactions, but needs access to information on all fatalities if it is to have effective oversight of food safety.
links.later_quote: In my opinion action should be taken to consider establishing a national reporting system which includes timely reporting to local authority and FSA and maintenance of a register of fatalities and their investigations, and consideration be given to investigating the feasibility of wider access to AAIs.
links.promise_quote: The FSA has started work on a project designed to collect more reported data on food-based allergic reactions that do not result in death. Work on this project is progressing despite some disruption due to the COVID-19 pandemic. We are currently undertaking discovery work with people with allergies to understand the type of information they could provide and the data that the FSA could receive on allergic reactions. This will enable us to assess expectations and the perceived usefulness of such
